dimensions.assessment: Affects all future purchasers and occupants of new motor vehicles with electronic door latches, as well as vehicle manufacturers.
dimensions.evidence: require each new motor vehicle to be equipped with a manual door release allowing timely exit regardless of failure of any electrical system

dimensions.assessment: Provides life-saving egress capability during electrical system failures, representing a notable safety enhancement for affected vehicles.
dimensions.evidence: a power independent, easy-to-find manual release for each door providing occupant egress, which shall be intuitive to use

dimensions.assessment: The source text does not state any federal spending amounts, appropriations, or specific economic compliance costs.
Amends title 49 of the United States Code by adding a specific new safety standard requirement administered by the Secretary of Transportation.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 49, United States Code, to require each new motor vehicle to be equipped with a manual door release

dimensions.assessment: Imposes a permanent design and manufacturing requirement for all future new motor vehicles meeting the criteria.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary of Transportation shall issue a final rule

missing_information: Estimated manufacturing cost per vehicle or total economic impact on the automotive industry.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates a vehicle safety standard change requiring all new motor vehicles with electronic door latches to include a power-independent manual release.
